core_obligations: Part (1) (proof lines 4074-4075): for an affine open U the retrocompactness of the complement gives a finitely generated ideal defining the closed subset Z cap U.

Part (2) (proof lines 4076-4090): over an affine open U = Spec(A) the module is attached to an A-module M, and a section x is supported in Z cap U exactly when x vanishes in every localization at a prime outside Z; by the support lemma this is equivalent to the support of x being contained in V(I), which for a finitely generated I is equivalent to I^n x = 0 for some n.

Part (3) (proof lines 4092-4106): for every open U the defining condition fits into the exact sequence 0 -> F'(U) -> F(U) -> F(U minus Z), and the last term is the sections of the pushforward of the restriction of F along the inclusion of the complement; that pushforward is quasi-coherent because the inclusion is quasi-compact and separated, so F' is the kernel of a map of quasi-coherent modules over a scheme, hence quasi-coherent.
proof_roadmap: Use retrocompactness to produce finitely generated ideals on affine opens.
Translate the support condition into annihilation by a power of that ideal using the support lemma.
Exhibit the sheaf as the kernel of a map to a quasi-coherent pushforward.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a closed subset Z of a scheme X with retrocompact complement and a quasi-coherent module F, the subsheaf of sections supported on Z is described on affine opens by annihilation by a power of a finitely generated ideal and is quasi-coherent (statement lines 4051-4072). The proof (proof lines 4074-4108) uses the finitely generated ideal on affine opens, translates the support condition through the support lemma, and identifies the sheaf as the kernel of a map to a quasi-coherent pushforward. H2: three parts with three inputs, written out in full.
